name: Silicone / onion extract scar gel (Mederma)

lead: Mederma is a popular OTC scar gel built around onion extract. Silicone gels and sheets are similar products.
Trials have generally not found it better than petrolatum.

paras: Claimed to soften scars; a rabbit study found improved collagen organization without significant size reduction.
Safety data are limited in the sources reviewed; the product contains alcohol and fragrance.

web.title: Silicone / onion extract scar gel (Mederma) — Grokipedia

lead: Mederma is an over-the-counter gel marketed to make scars look softer and less noticeable; its name-giving ingredient is onion bulb extract, and the listed active ingredient is allantoin [1]. Silicone gels and sheets are a related class of topical scar products.

Studies have mostly not favored Mederma over basic treatments. Two trials found onion extract gel no better than petrolatum, and a rabbit ear study found no significant reduction in scar size, height or inflammation [1][2][3].

paras: A 2006 prospective double-blinded study compared onion extract gel with a petrolatum emollient on new surgical scars [3]. A 2002 rabbit ear model study noted that little scientific evidence existed for Mederma on hypertrophic scars [2]. Wikipedia reports a 2006 trial found no significant difference from petrolatum [1].
For hypertrophic scars, Wikipedia says silicone gel sheeting may slightly improve appearance compared with onion extract, though whether it beats other methods is uncertain [4].

Registered trials include a post-surgical scar study of Mederma [5], a randomized comparison of two topical therapies for keloids and hypertrophic scars [6], and a study of OTC scar-management modalities [7].
A 1998 Archives of Dermatology essay discussed dermatology and the marketing of skin products [8].

timeline.event: Rabbit ear model study of Mederma published [2].
HRA Pharma buys the brand; Perrigo acquires HRA in 2021 [1].
